notes: Correction: מֵאֵת (s013-s014) is now one unit on the single word from, headed on מִן. Rule 23 names מֵאֵת as a compound preposition whose source head is the governing morpheme standing first, and rule 30 forbids leaving one member unrepresented beside another that holds the whole rendering. The neighbouring מִבֵּין pairs are split, correctly, because there the ASV writes a word for each morpheme (from between).

Both articles on הַמִּזְבֵּחַ take the ASV's his under rule 41, which reads a possessive standing in the article's slot as what the article is rendered by; no suffix stands in the Hebrew, so rule 18's closing sentence does not reach the word.
מִבֵּין is written twice in the Hebrew and once in English: the second preposition and its בֵּין are unrepresented under rule 26.
